auth.notes: Owner account plus developer API credentials for the public export helper. Endpoints and real output are deliberately not reproduced.

cloud.failure_mode: First-time provisioning and fresh credential export stop without the vendor service. A replacement client that already holds all four values performs status and legacy challenge-response locally over BLE without further cloud contact. Firmware download and credential rotation/reissue remain cloud dependent; acceptance after rotation or on ID2-only firmware is unknown.
cloud.notes: The v1 lock itself has no Wi-Fi/LAN path. The service dependency is bootstrap, not a claim that every later BLE session is cloud-routed.
cloud.vendor_service: Wyze account/device service, required for initial provisioning and owner credential export

identity.notes: The account UUID is secret credential material and is never logged; retain it in a secret store. Re-resolve a changed BLE address through the owner record rather than guessing from a scan.

discovery.none: Manual selection only. Do not auto-identify from NUS, an advertisement name, company ID 0xFFFF or a bare address. The address is a connection locator supplied by the owner's device record, not public proof of model. Wyze Lock Bolt v2 and other Yunding devices are excluded.

distributors.notes: Protocol and hardware platform partner named by the v1 quick-start guide; not an assertion that other Lockin products are compatible.

identification.notes: Deliberately empty of executable matchers. The vendor's normal connection flow resolves a provisioned lock by its account-associated BLE address, not by an advertised model name. NUS is shared with unrelated devices; manufacturer ID 0xFFFF is not a Wyze assignment. Manually select WLCKB1 and confirm Device Information plus marker-valid encrypted status.

device.name: Wyze Lock Bolt v1 (WLCKB1)
device.notes:
SCOPE IS v1 ONLY. Wyze Lock Bolt v2 adds Wi-Fi and is a different product; do not apply this BLE credential or frame profile to it. The older Wyze Lock, the separate Lock Bolt Keypad, gateways and other Yunding products are also out of scope.
Consumer integration is identify_only and manual-selection-only. Nordic UART Service (NUS) is a shared byte transport, never Wyze identity. A scan must not select this spec from NUS, an unknown name or manufacturer data. The owner selects WLCKB1 explicitly, supplies that lock's exported address and credentials, and a dedicated handler validates encrypted status before any write. There are no generic entities or executable command bindings.
Once the owner has exported the cloud device UUID, 32-character BLE token, numeric BLE key id and lock address, later operation is local BLE without cloud access. The UUID's last 16 ASCII characters decrypt state/door/ battery. The token's last 16 ASCII characters are the legacy operate key. These are account-bound per-lock secrets: keep them out of logs, docs, diagnostics and shell history. Initial provisioning/export still requires the vendor cloud; no offline credential-issuance path is claimed.

openness.notes: No official local protocol document was found. Public implementations and the vendor codec agree on the legacy wire format; current-firmware acceptance of legacy versus ID2 remains unverified.

enter_pairing_mode.indicator: Three beeps and a white flashing keypad after releasing the P button.

procedures.basis: Official Wyze Lock Bolt v1 setup guide, updated 2025-03-24; not replayed here.

steps.action: Select the v1 Lock Bolt in the official app with Internet and Bluetooth enabled.
Press and hold the round P button under the batteries, then release when the lock gives three beeps and the keypad flashes white.
steps.expect: The app finds and connects to the v1 lock. Do not remove a battery during pairing.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app/other central and reconnect with the cached owner values; do not erase users/settings to resolve a busy link.

pairing.notes: Pairing is application-layer provisioning, not an established OS BLE bond. Later sessions use the exported secrets and challenge-response; no PIN or bond flow is asserted for a replacement client.

unpair.clears: The account binding and stored setup state; treat old exported credentials as invalid and re-provision.
unpair.notes: There is no unpair short of the official Delete Device factory reset; a plain OS Bluetooth 'forget' action is not the provisioning reset.

safety_advisory.detail: Keep a person at the door with the independent mechanical entry method available. Complete a fresh challenge, send at most one intentional command, require the result/ACK and validate the subsequent encrypted state notification. Never replay a timed-out actuation automatically, fall back to ID2, or expose either operation as a one-tap generic entity.
safety_advisory.summary: Legacy lock/unlock moves a real deadbolt. It is advanced and attended only; NUS discovery, a timeout or an automatic scan must never actuate it.

factory_reset.description: Official v1 factory reset is Delete Device in the Wyze app while in BLE range, confirmed by a short series of beeps. Removing/reinserting one battery is only a power cycle. Do not power-cycle during the pairing period: official guidance warns that pairing-button plus battery removal can delete all users and settings.
factory_reset.effect: Returns the lock to new-device setup. Treat stored users/settings and previously exported client credentials as no longer usable; exact key rotation is not established. Re-provision and export fresh values.

procedures.basis: Official Wyze v1 factory-reset guide, updated 2024-05-02; not executed by this project.
procedures.indicator: A short series of beeps confirms the reset.
procedures.name: Delete the v1 lock in the official app

steps.action: Keep the door attended and move within Bluetooth range of the v1 lock.
In the Wyze app open the v1 lock and choose Settings, then Delete Device.
steps.expect: A short beep series confirms factory reset; set the lock up as a new device and export fresh credentials.

steps.action: Do not remove a battery during pairing; if only a power cycle is intended, stop and use the separate battery power-cycle procedure instead.

cloud.local_alternative: No offline first-time credential issuance is known. Later sessions need only the cached per-lock UUID, token, BLE key id and address.

methods.description: A staged owner route: official v1 setup and credential export once, then a dedicated local handler using only the cached values. The public extraction helper's account/API prerequisites are a boundary, not something this project ran or reproduces.
methods.name: Provision/export once, then use cached credentials locally

steps.action: Install v1 WLCKB1 with four AA batteries, enable Bluetooth and Internet access, and stay within about 16 feet of the lock.
In the Wyze app select the v1 Lock Bolt, then press and hold the round P button under the batteries until release produces three beeps and a white flashing keypad.
steps.expect: The app connects and completes initial v1 setup; do not confuse this with the Wi-Fi-capable v2.

steps.action: Through an owner-authorized account export, privately record the device UUID, BLE token, numeric BLE key id and lock address in a secret store; never paste them into shared logs.
steps.expect: All four values are available offline. The UUID/token suffixes are not printed or committed.

steps.action: Manually select WLCKB1, connect and subscribe to UART/state, read Device Information, and require a 16-byte encrypted status block to decrypt with zero padding and ASCII loock at bytes 11..15.
steps.expect: Read-only status and battery validate. Stop on another model, bad marker/padding or an ID2-only dialect; do not send actuation.

causes: Battery 0x2A19 is not a plain SIG byte here: decrypt exactly one AES block with the UUID suffix and require the marker and zero padding.
The selected device may not be the provisioned v1, or the exported UUID/address may belong to another lock.
troubleshooting.symptom: A generic battery reader returns nonsense or status decryption fails.

causes: Current firmware may require the unresolved ID2 path. Do not retry with guessed CCM parameters or replay the legacy command; capture owner-authorized read-only traffic first.

causes: Close the other central, use an active Bluetooth proxy if range is poor, and re-check the owner-supplied address rather than identifying every NUS advertiser.

setup.notes: First-time provisioning needs the Wyze app, Internet access and the account-backed device record. Official setup uses the physical P button under the batteries. A replacement client needs the four exported values above. After that, cloud-free local BLE works until credentials are rotated/revoked; actual longevity on current firmware is unverified.

rejoin.notes: There is no Wi-Fi network on v1. A client holding the current exported values reconnects over BLE without cloud access. A new client needs an owner-authorized export; loss/rotation of those values requires the vendor account, not an automatic factory reset.

steps.action: Close the previous central and select the exact provisioned WLCKB1 manually.
Reconnect with cached credentials and validate read-only status before any write; fetch fresh values only if the lock rejects them.

testing.notes: No Wyze lock, owner account, real key material or BLE capture was used. L1/L2 framing, encrypted status and legacy challenge-response come from the reviewed vendor protocol codec, cross-checked against the pinned public local integrations. Public implementation success is reported evidence, not a hardware run by this project. ID2 firmware selection is unresolved and no ID2 actuation is offered.

local_access.summary: Phone-direct encrypted BLE after one owner-authorized cloud export. identify_only here until a consumer implements strict status validation and the legacy session handler.

EncryptedStatusBlock.description: Sixteen-byte AES-128-ECB plaintext shared by lock state, door state and battery reads.

fields.description: Raw state or battery percent; 0xFF unknown
fields.name: payload

parse_rules: Decrypt exactly one block using device_uuid[-16:] as 16 ASCII key bytes; never use the BLE token for status.
Require bytes 5..10 zero and bytes 11..15 ASCII loock before using payload/timestamp.
Interpret lock payload 0 as unlocked, 1 as locked, 0xFF as unknown; battery accepts only 0..100 or unknown.

consumer_limitations.required_handler: Manual WLCKB1 selection + strict encrypted-status validation + legacy challenge/session sequencing + advanced attended confirmation.

id2_unresolved.reported_algorithm: Fold challenge[0:8] XOR challenge[8:16] into an 8-byte AES-CCM nonce, encrypt the same operation marker with the legacy operate-key suffix, and carry plaintext marker under key 0x0111 before CCM protection.
id2_unresolved.status: documentary only; not implemented and not a fallback
id2_unresolved.unknowns: Accepted firmware, exact CCM tag/parameters and complete field ordering are not capture-confirmed. Do not construct or send an ID2 operation from this outline.

l1_transport.ack: An ACK has flags 0x08 and empty payload. Its eight-byte header still contains the CRC of empty input, 0x0000.

layout.name: flags
layout.values: 0x00 client request; 0x08 ACK; 0x40 device data; 0x48 device ACK+data

l1_transport.reassembly: Scan to 0xAB, retain incomplete frames, validate declared length and CRC before delivery. On bad magic/CRC discard through the bad frame and rescan at the next 0xAB; never deliver a corrupt payload.
l1_transport.sequencing: Challenge request sequence 1, legacy actuation sequence 2. ACK echoes the data frame's sequence. Sequence is a uint16 counter; overflow behavior is not asserted.

l2_payload.header: command uint8, version_flags uint8. High nibble 0 selects legacy one-byte TLV keys; high nibble 7 selects ID2 two-byte big-endian TLV keys.
l2_payload.id2_tlv: key uint16 BE | length uint16 BE | value[length]. Syntax documentation only; no ID2 actuation implementation is declared.
l2_payload.legacy_tlv: key uint8 | length uint16 BE | value[length]
l2_payload.validation: Require the full two-byte header and exact TLV lengths, reject truncation/duplicate keys, and reject an unsupported version nibble rather than guessing.

algorithm: Start with the 0x91 challenge request and require its ACK plus command 0x86 / field 0xD2 with a fresh 16-byte challenge.
operate_key = ASCII bytes of ble_token[16:32]. Require a 32-character token and a 16-byte challenge.
response = AES-128-ECB-encrypt(operate_key, challenge), no padding. XOR each byte with the 16-byte operation marker: byte0=0x01 unlock or 0x02 lock, bytes1..10 zero, bytes11..15 ASCII loock.

Build legacy L2 command 0x04/version 0x00 with key 0x05 = numeric BLE key id uint16 BE, key 0x04 = 16-byte response, then key 0xAD=00, key 0xF4=01 and key 0xF7=01 (each one-byte value). Preserve this field order.
Wrap in L1 with flags 0 and sequence 2. Send once; require data/result handling and ACK as documented, then require a marker-valid state notification. Never auto-replay after timeout.
result_sequence: The public client expects challenge ACK flags 0x48 / sequence 1, then device data flags 0x40.
ACK each device data frame with flags 0x08 and its sequence. Command ACK may be absent on some firmware; a command 0x04 result is the alternative, not a reason to resend.
Wait for encrypted state notification. Treat absent notification as a later read-back requirement, never as permission to send the operation again.
legacy_actuation.scope: Documentary for a dedicated handler only. Do not execute unless v1 was manually selected, read-only status validated, the user is attending, and legacy support is confirmed.

characteristics.name: Battery level (AES-encrypted, not plain SIG uint8)
characteristics.notes: Exactly 16 ciphertext bytes. Decrypt with the last 16 ASCII characters of the device UUID; require bytes 5..10 zero and bytes 11..15 ASCII loock. Byte 0 is percent 0..100; 0xFF means unknown. Timestamp is uint32 BE seconds at 1..4.
